- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates downside; add buffer below forecast or adjust downward more aggressively.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply decay or smoothing to subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; prioritize sentiment-driven reversion in 3–5 day horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; apply upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish, and downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish.
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (±0.33), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance or add stochastic adjustment.
- Forecast should not be linearly extrapolated from recent history; incorporate sentiment-weighted moving average or sentiment-adjusted trend filter.
